name: Update Entity NBT
desc: Updates the NBT data of an entity (used for command block minecarts, spawned entities with custom NBT).

writeup.p: The server pushes a full NBTTagCompound onto a specific entity: an entity id as VarInt followed by a compound NBT tag. EntityTrackerEntry sends it when a tracked entity holds NBT the client must know (command block minecarts, boats with custom names, armor stands) and a new player starts tracking it. Clientbound-only, PLAY state.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleUpdateEntityNBT looks up the entity by id and calls readFromNBT with the compound; unknown ids are ignored. Server side, the send is triggered inside EntityTrackerEntry's update loop when the tracked entity's NBT differs for the tracking player, typically on track start. The client never requests this packet.

No module in the 8 clients intercepts S49; modules is empty here because the corpus contains no module file for it. The only non-vanilla reference is the Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 NetworkAPI script registry. The command-block NBT exploit lore lives server-side: a client cannot read a command block's NBT through this packet, because the server only pushes NBT it already chose to send. It is a one-way data push with no client-visible lever.

The compound is decoded client-side by the NBT reader; a hostile compound with pathological nesting or huge size is the only theoretical surface, and no client in the corpus defends against it. There is no spoofing, replay or timing angle for modules: the entity id must match a known entity and the payload is applied verbatim.

implementation.overview: A server-pushed entity NBT update with no module coverage: modules is empty because the corpus has no module file for S49. The only non-vanilla hit is the Rise 6.x NetworkAPI script registry; the command-block NBT exploit is server-side, and the packet itself offers clients nothing to hook.
implementation.server_handling: EntityTrackerEntry sends S49 when the tracked entity's NBT differs for the tracking player, normally at track start (the entry's sendMetadata loop). The client applies the compound via readFromNBT on the resolved entity. No reply, no ownership validation, no client-triggered path.
implementation.protocol_notes: A VarInt entity id followed by a full NBT compound written through writeTag. Sizes are unbounded by the protocol beyond the packet limit; command block minecart compounds carry the command string, which is the data of interest in the exploit lore. The packet id 0x49 is clientbound-only.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats ignore this packet entirely, and clients cannot abuse it because the server controls both the trigger and the payload. The only measurable property is packet size, which is server-controlled.
implementation.general_hooks: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 expose S49 to scripts through NetworkAPI's packet registry; no event bus in any of the 8 clients has a module handler for it.
implementation.client_variations: Only Rise 6.x differs from vanilla: its NetworkAPI packet list includes S49PacketUpdateEntityNBT.class. All other clients carry the unmodified NetHandlerPlayClient handler.
